prompt: From comma-separated sales lines, find each region's best-selling product (ties going to the alphabetically smaller name) and rank every product by total revenue descending. Complete both methods in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Both answers start from the same shape: split each line, then group and total with Collectors.summingLong. Picking a winner per region needs a nested groupingBy so each region has its own product-to-revenue map, and then a comparator that sorts by value descending and falls back to the key ascending -- Map.Entry.comparingByValue(Comparator.reverseOrder()).thenComparing(Map.Entry.comparingByKey()). Using max with a hand-rolled comparator is tempting but gets the tie wrong, because max keeps the LAST maximum it sees for equal elements rather than the alphabetically smallest.
hints: Map each line to its String[] parts once at the top of the pipeline; everything downstream can then read parts[0], parts[1] and parts[2].
Collectors.groupingBy(region, TreeMap::new, Collectors.groupingBy(product, Collectors.summingLong(...))) gives you a region-to-product-to-total map in a single collect.
Build the tie-break as one comparator: Map.Entry.comparingByValue(Comparator.reverseOrder()).thenComparing(Map.Entry.comparingByKey()), then sorted(...) and take the first entry per region.
